steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Identify a genuine citizenship issue: something related to rights, democracy, equality, or community participation that you care about and that affects real people.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Research the issue thoroughly using reliable sources: government statistics, charity reports, academic research, surveys, and expert interviews. Avoid relying on social media alone.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Set SMART targets: Specific (clear and focused), Measurable (can track progress), Achievable (realistic given your resources), Relevant (linked to citizenship), Time-bound (with deadlines).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Identify stakeholders: who is affected by the issue, who has the power to change it, and who might support or oppose your action. Understanding power dynamics is key.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What are the key stages in planning a citizenship action? | Q: Why is it important to identify stakeholders when planning citizenship action? | Q: Give an example of a SMART target for a citizenship action.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 1) Identify a citizenship issue, 2) Research the issue thoroughly, 3) Set clear aims and SMART targets, 4) Decide on methods and actions, 5) Plan resources, timescales, and roles, 6) Carry out the act | Stakeholders are the people or groups affected by or with power over the issue. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: AQA Paper 2 Section B asks about your citizenship action — prepare detailed notes in advance Always link your action to citizenship concepts (rights, democracy, participation, equality) Evaluation is worth the most marks — explain what worked, what didn't, and why
